title.narrative: Partnership Framework with the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) 2022-2025

description.narrative: The United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) is the UN agency overseeing implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030. It supports countries to implement the Sendai Framework (and the Sendai Gender Action Plan, which shares best practice) to prevent new and reduce existing disaster risks and to strengthen resilience through a multi-hazard approach to disaster risk management. UNDRR also supports strengthening inclusivity and resilience through the Early Warnings for All Initiative. This investment’s core funding enables UNDRR to implement its Strategic Partnership Framework with Australia, the approach and objectives of which include mobilising advocacy and knowledge sharing for risk-informed sustainable development; capacity building to increase the availability of risk data and information; and strengthening inclusive disaster resilience in the Pacific reg of the partnership also support UNDRR’s work in the Indo-Pacific region.

description.narrative: As part of the Making Cities Resilient 2030 (MCR2030) initiative, UNDRR developed the Annex for Inclusion of Persons with Disabilities to the Disaster Resilience Scorecard for Cities. By the end of 2023, 588 cities in 15 countries in Asia and the Pacific had signed up to MCR2030 with 240 million people living in these cities. This tool helps local governments assess and strengthen strategies for disability-inclusive disaster risk reduction and includes persons with disabilities in development and implementation of the strategies. Following training on the toolkit in Bhutan, local authorities improved public transport accessibility for persons with disabilities, boosting their resilience and collection of disability-disaggregated data to address the specific needs during disasters. UNDRR’s 2023 Global Survey on Persons with Disabilities and Disasters, based on 5,717 responses from 137 countries, indicated that limited progress has been made over the past decade and underlines the opportunities for investment to accelerate progress.

description.narrative: In 2023, UNDRR and partners introduced anticipatory action approaches to governments and regional organizations in the Pacific region as a key preparatory tool to prevent and/or mitigate disaster impacts. UNDRR initiated and co-led the first Pacific Anticipatory Action Week. Recognising the value of an anticipatory action approach, the Government of Fiji, with UNDRR’s support, subsequently established the first national framework for anticipatory action, linking early warnings to early action to protect people and livelihoods. The institutionalization of AA within the existing disaster risk management system will ensure sustainability. Moreover, the first parametric insurance scheme in the Pacific region, supported by UNDRR, now provides farming groups in Fiji with funds to act early in case of cyclones.

The Sendai Framework Gender Action Plan (Sendai GAP), launched in March 2024, is a pivotal step towards gender responsiveness and a human rights-based approach to disaster risk reduction (DRR). Developed through a comprehensive consultation process with governments and non-governmental stakeholders from different regions, the Sendai GAP is an important step towards strengthening the normative frameworks for DRR. Co-led by UNDRR, UNWOMEN, and UNFPA, the development involved diverse groups, among others the Asia-Pacific Gender Stakeholder Group, Shifting the Power Coalition (Pacific) and the Women’s International Network for DRR. Australia has supported the implementation of the Sendai GAP, including by building capacity and strengthening advocacy in countries, the United Nations and with key stakeholders.

UNDRR has supported countries in Asia-Pacific in the development and implementation of national disaster risk reduction strategies, plans and governance. Example, convened by UNDRR and hosted by the Government of Australia, the Asia-Pacific Ministerial Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction provided countries to call on governments to contribute to the Sendai Framework Midterm Review and improved DRR governance. This resulted in an increase of stakeholder engagement across all sectors and society to advance the localization of DRR by ensuring collaboration and increased reporting on the Midterm review in Asia-Pacific region by all 13 countries managed by UNDRR for this investment.
